course.title: React Native — Complete Deep Mobile Development Course
course.description: A React Native-specific, beginner-to-advanced mobile development course with detailed UI, state, networking, persistence, authentication, testing, performance and production release lessons.
course.curriculumPolicy: Module and lesson counts are determined by the concepts required to learn the platform properly; no fixed cross-mobile template is imposed.
learningOutcomes: Test, optimize and prepare production releases.
Build a complete learning-platform mobile client.

modules.title: React Native Foundations
modules.description: React Native architecture, project structure, JavaScript/TypeScript, native rendering and development workflow.

lessons.title: React Native Foundations
lessons.description: React Native architecture, project structure, JavaScript/TypeScript, native rendering and development workflow.
learningObjectives: Apply it to a real mobile learning workflow.
Handle state, lifecycle and errors correctly.

notes.text: React Native architecture, project structure, JavaScript/TypeScript, native rendering and development workflow.
Learn react native foundations by understanding the mobile-app problem first, then the framework concept, then a small implementation, and finally how it fits into a production learning application.

React Native Foundations is important when building a reliable mobile learning experience. Students should understand not only how to make the screen work, but also state, lifecycle, networking, performance, accessibility and production behavior.

notes.alt: React Native React Native Foundations visual
notes.caption: Add a mobile architecture or UI diagram showing React Native Foundations visually.

items: Handle loading, empty and error states.

notes.code:
Scenario: Create the foundation of a mobile learning app.

Flow: user action -> UI state -> application logic -> data source -> result -> updated UI.

items: Define the state and data boundary.
Test loading, success and failure states.
Test different screen sizes and accessibility.
Putting all state into one component.
Blocking the UI with synchronous work.
Building only for one screen size.
Keep UI and data responsibilities separated.
I can explain React Native Foundations in my own words.
I can implement a small example.
I can explain the data/state flow.
I can handle a failure state.
I can explain one production concern.
